chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whichever believer has an obstruction between him and another believer, Allah will place between him and Paradise seventy thousand walls; the thickness of each wall is a journey of a thousand years, and the distance from one wall to the next is a journey of a thousand years.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of creating an obstruction between believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the gravity of 'hijab'—spiritual or relational obstruction—between believers. The vivid imagery of seventy thousand walls, each with a thickness and distance of a thousand years' journey, underscores the immense spiritual barrier erected by neglecting brotherly ties, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethics regarding social cohesion. This serves as a stern warning that interpersonal discord can delay or obstruct one's ultimate entry into Paradise.
